title: Beyond the 956: Peggy King, 'George Gobel Show' singer and star of television's golden age, dies at 96
excerpt: Peggy King, the 1950s television and recording star known as "Pretty Perky Peggy King" on "The George Gobel Show," has died at 96 after a battle with Alzheimer's disease. Her publicist confirmed her death on Sunday, October 25, 2026.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Peggy King, the 1950s television and recording star known to a generation of viewers as "Pretty Perky Peggy King" on "The George Gobel Show," has died at 96.

King died on Sunday, October 25, 2026, after a battle with Alzheimer's disease at the Saunders House assisted living facility in Wynnewood, Pennsylvania. Her publicist, Alan Eicher, confirmed her death.

Born February 16, 1930, in Greensburg, Pennsylvania, King began singing on radio in Cleveland before touring with the big bands of Charlie Spivak, Ray Anthony and Ralph Flanagan. She signed with MGM in 1952, leading to a singing cameo in Vincente Minnelli's film "The Bad and the Beautiful."

Her national breakthrough came as a regular on "The George Gobel Show" from 1954 to 1957, where host George Gobel gave her the nickname that stayed with her for the rest of her career. She was nominated for an Emmy Award for best female singer in 1955, performed "Count Your Blessings" at the 1955 Academy Awards and co-hosted the Emmy Awards in 1958.

As a recording artist, she signed a long-term contract with Columbia Records, where she released the best-selling albums "Wish Upon a Star" and "Girl Meets Boy." DownBeat and Billboard named her best new singer for 1955-56. She also appeared on "The Bob Hope Show," "American Bandstand," "The Steve Allen Show," "The Jack Benny Program" and "The Perry Como Show," and guest-starred on "Maverick" and "Dragnet."

King received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on February 8, 1960, among the first entertainers honored, and was inducted into the Broadcast Pioneers Hall of Fame in 2010. She returned to performing in later years, singing with the All-Star Jazz Trio.

She is survived by her daughter, Suzy Rudofker, and son-in-law, Dwain Goforth.

Sources: Variety; publicist Alan Eicher; The Spun.
